sections.description: Bliss frames the talk around becoming the 'human duct tape' who can drive customer-focused work. She critiques memos and generic slogans and emphasizes breaking work into manageable pieces while uniting leaders with frontline teams to deliver a consistent, customer-centered experience.
sections.title: Opening: From memos to deliberate customer focus

sections.description: The speaker argues against silo-driven, heroic frontline efforts and highlights the importance of removing back-end frictions. She introduces the idea of touching points and the need to map and prioritize a small set of critical moments (10-15) to deliver reliability where it matters most.
sections.title: Reliability over wow moments; breaking down barriers

sections.description: Bliss ties historical development of customer experience to real-world examples. She cites SAS Airlines and Jan Carlson’s work on moments of truth, Lands’ End’s growth via journey thinking, and Amazon’s reliability-driven growth as demonstrations of the framework in action.
sections.title: Roots, case studies, and the idea of customer assets

sections.description: The keynote introduces the main framework: five competencies to lead customer experience. She discusses treating customers as assets, naming journey stages, building a listening path, and storytelling. A preview of the upcoming book and the concept of a Vulcan mind meld for reality-checks in leadership discussions are included.
sections.title: Five competencies and the preview of Chief Customer Officer 2.0

sections.description: The final section covers Competencies 3-5, focusing on building a robust listening path, preempting unreliability, and establishing accountability and governance. Bliss describes practical governance tools like the customer room, immersive leadership experiences (Adobe), and a recipe-card approach to executive actions, plus the need for corporate patience as a cultural lever.
sections.title: Competencies 3-5: listening, reliability, and accountability; operational governance

summary: Jeanne Bliss presents a practical framework for turning customer-centric rhetoric into a repeatable, revenue-driving growth engine. She argues that most organizations are siloed and deliver inconsistent experiences unless work is broken into bite-sized, cross-functional efforts focused on reliable performance in the moments that matter. The talk traces roots of the discipline (moments of truth) through SAS Airlines, Lands’ End, and other case studies, then introduces five competencies for leading a customer-centric organization: treating customers as assets, defining journey stages, building a disciplined listening path, preempting unreliability, and ensuring leadership accountability. She peppered the talk with concrete tactics (touchpoint mapping, ‘kill a stupid rule,’ the customer room, storytelling by stage, and Vulcan mind meld exercises) and illustrated how reliability precedes delight, how to converge customer data into actionable insights, and how to structure governance to sustain a culture of customer growth.
title: Building a Customer-Driven Growth Engine: Jeannie Bliss on Reliability, Moments of Truth, and Five Competencies
